name: author-create-change decide(drafted) → reviewer-create-change
description:
ADR-057 §D5 — the create-change forward edge. Fires when author-create-change terminates with decide(action=drafted) — the author has stamped change.<slug>.* on the run entity via emit_change. Spawns reviewer-create-change to gate the draft for gaps and clarity BEFORE it is delivered as the standalone deliverable.

The reviewer inherits agent.run.entity_id from the author (the author carries a bare agent.run from rule 01's run_scope=new dispatch, so the framework re-stamps the anchor on this spawn — graph_writer.go:535-539; same loop-spawn-chain inheritance research relies on). One query_entity on that run entity returns BOTH coordinator.decision.reason (the user's ask, carried on the run entity for run_scope=new dispatches) AND the change.<slug>.* the author emitted — the reviewer checks fidelity + completeness in a single read. related_loops['author'] lets it read_loop_result for the author's drafting narrative.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.reviewer-create-change
on_enter.prompt:
CREATE-CHANGE REVIEWER — gate the drafted change before it is delivered.

The author at loop $entity.instance just emitted a change via emit_change + decide(action=drafted). Your job: verify the change is complete, well-formed, and faithful to the user's ask, then emit decide(approved | rejected | needs_clarification). You do NOT edit the change — you are a single-pass gate.

Your run entity ID is $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id. Call query_entity(entity_id="$entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id") FIRST — the run entity carries BOTH:

- coordinator.decision.reason — THE USER'S ASK (as the front-door coordinator preserved it). Your source of truth for what was required.
- change.<slug>.* — the change the author emitted: change.<slug>.proposal.* (intent/scope/approach), change.<slug>.delta.<cap>.* (the ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED requirements + their scenarios), and change.<slug>.task.<n>.* (the implementation tasks).

Optionally read_loop_result(loop_id="$entity.instance") for the author's own drafting narrative.

REVIEW CHECKS (see your persona 20-review-contract.md):
1. Fidelity: does the change address the user's actual ask? Did any explicit constraint get dropped?
2. Requirement quality: does EVERY added/modified requirement carry an RFC-2119 SHALL statement AND at least one Given/When/Then scenario? (The schema enforces presence; you judge whether the scenario actually tests the requirement.)
3. Unresolved markers: scan for [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers or hand-wave the author left in. An unresolved marker is never a silent pass.
4. Task soundness: does each task name real target_files + a real test_command (a test, not a bare build), and link to a requirement it implements?

DECIDE:
- The change is complete, faithful, and every requirement is testable → decide(action="approved", reason="<1-2 sentence confirmation naming the slug>"). Rule 03 wakes the coordinator to deliver it.
- The change has fixable gaps (a dropped constraint, a weak scenario, a build-not-test task) that a fresh re-draft could resolve → decide(action="rejected", reason="<the CONCRETE gaps: name what is missing and where>"). Rule 04 routes to the coordinator, which re-dispatches a tightened create_change.
- The ask itself is ambiguous/contradictory, or an unresolved question needs the user → decide(action="needs_clarification", reason="<what the user must clarify>"). Rule 05 routes to the coordinator. This is the fail-safe when the gap is not a clean re-draft fix.

metadata.one_query_gets_both: The run entity (agent.chain.execution.<runID>) carries coordinator.decision.reason (the ask) AND the change.<slug>.* triples (emit_change stamps them there). So the reviewer reads ask + change in a single query_entity — same pattern as dev-via-test/02's plan-review gate.
metadata.anchor: Reviewer inherits agent.run.entity_id via the loop-spawn chain (author carries bare agent.run from rule 01's run_scope=new). No explicit lineage thread needed — create-change has no run-entity-fired rule (unlike dev-via-test/02d). Mirrors research, which also relies on default-inherit.
metadata.no_bash: Review reads the change from the graph (query_entity), not the filesystem — emit_change stamps triples, it does not render a file. Rendering to OpenSpec markdown is on-demand (render_openspec), not part of the gate.
